purpose: Use carefully argued original texts to specify faithful reconstruction, not to assume that every author commits a fallacy.

cases.author: Edmund L. Gettier
cases.title: Is Justified True Belief Knowledge?
cases.locator: Printed pp. 121-122: initial assumptions and Case I
semantic_requirements: Separate actual-world truth from a subject's belief and justification.
Record the evidence and inference supporting a belief.
Track which object makes an existential description true.
Attribute the proposed knowledge analysis to the target view, not to Gettier's conclusion.
cases.positive_control: Preserve the difference between the valid embedded deduction and the challenge to a proposed sufficient condition for knowledge.
cases.mutation_control: A reconstruction that makes justification factive changes the source assumptions and must be flagged.
cases.generation_constraint: Never count a free assignment of Knowledge=false as discovery of a conceptual counterexample; knowledge attribution needs a declared interpretive judgment or reviewed case label.

cases.author: Thomas Nagel
cases.title: What Is It Like to Be a Bat?
cases.locator: Printed pp. 439-442, especially notes 6 and 8; p. 446 on the conclusion about physicalism
semantic_requirements: Preserve the experiencer and the perspective from which a description is understood.
Distinguish first-person understanding from externally available physical description.
Preserve qualifications concerning current explanatory understanding.
Distinguish an epistemic or explanatory difficulty from the falsity of an ontological thesis.
cases.positive_control: Do not report physicalism as refuted merely because the reconstructed text records an explanatory gap.
cases.mutation_control: Strengthening a qualified explanatory conclusion into an unrestricted impossibility or falsity claim must be identified as a changed argument.
cases.generation_constraint: No numerical or Boolean assignment alone adjudicates the phenomenological claim; unsupported semantics remain review-required.

cases.author: W. V. Quine
cases.title: On What There Is
cases.locator: Retyped PDF pp. 1 and 3-5: McX, Pegasus, and descriptive paraphrase; these are not original journal page numbers
semantic_requirements: Distinguish a quoted name, a purported referent, a mental representation and an existential commitment.
Track author versus opponent commitments and concessions for argument.
Make the denotation assumptions of the chosen formal language explicit.
Treat descriptive paraphrase as an explicit interpretation rather than silently introducing a denoting constant.
cases.positive_control: A reconstruction must permit discussion of a purported entity without silently settling the existence dispute.
cases.mutation_control: Moving McX's presupposition into Quine's accepted premises must be detected as an attribution error.
cases.generation_constraint: A model of one chosen regimentation is not by itself a resolution of all rival ontologies.

cases.author: W. V. Quine
cases.title: Two Dogmas of Empiricism
cases.locator: Sections I-III, especially the definition and interchangeability discussions
cases.edition_note: The host explicitly displays differences between the 1951 text and the revised 1961 version; record this rather than treating it as an unmarked original edition.
semantic_requirements: Distinguish sameness of reference or extension from synonymy.
Distinguish stipulative definitions from claims about established usage.
Preserve quotation and compound-expression boundaries during substitution.
Treat a concept mapping as an interpretation requiring grounds, not an automatic philosophical solution.
cases.positive_control: Do not assume that creating one concept identifier establishes cognitive synonymy.
cases.mutation_control: Applying an object-language synonym substitution inside a quotation or a different compound must be flagged for review.
cases.generation_constraint: Search over stated admissible readings, not arbitrary changes of meaning chosen solely to make the argument fail.
